sentences: The hero and his ward, secret government agents following the Japanese attack on the harbor, become aware of a Japanese sabotage ring operating in the city.
The hero's girlfriend asks for his help in finding her uncle, who was abducted by the ring after he was released from prison.
The doctor, the Japanese leader of the ring, plans to steal the city's radium supply to power his invention, a hand-held raygun that can dissolve anything hit by its powerful beam.
He forces the uncle to reveal the location of the vault where the radium is stored.
The doctor sends his American henchmen, along with a zombie that he controls by microphone via an electronic brain implant, to steal the precious metal.
The hero discovers the plot and eventually routs the gang after a battle.
In his secret base, the hero interrogates one of the doctor's henchmen, who reveals the radium was to have been taken to a building, located in the mostly deserted Japanese section of the city.
The hero and his ward infiltrate the gang's lair (also the doctor's laboratory), hidden inside a still-open business, a fun house ride.
There, they find the girlfriend bound, gagged, and unconscious.
After she is rescued by the duo, the doctor transforms her uncle into a zombie and plots the derailment of a heavily laden supply train.
Once again, the doctor's sabotage efforts are stopped by the hero and his ward.
Traps and counter-traps follow in the succeeding chapters, as the duo continue to thwart the plans of the Japanese agent and his henchmen.
The hero and his ward finally prevail, overseeing the capture of the doctor's men and finally the death of the Japanese agent as he tries to escape.
When the hero and his sidekick get a tip that a commodore, owner of a distillery, is in danger aboard his yacht, they launch a rescue mission using the helicopter.
As the hero descends on the ladder to land on the yacht, it suddenly vanishes beneath him.
He rises out of the sea with a shark attacking his leg.
After the hero dislodges it with shark repellent, the shark explodes.

The hero and his sidekick head back to the police commissioner's office, where they deduce that the tip was a set-up by a criminal alliance, a gathering of four of the most powerful villains in the city: three men and a woman.

The four criminals equip themselves with a dehydrator that can turn humans into dust until they are rehydrated (an invention of the commodore's, who is unaware that he has been kidnapped), escape in a war-surplus, pre-atomic submarine made to resemble a penguin, and recruit three pirate-themed henchmen.

The hero and his sidekick learn that the yacht was really a holographic projection and return via boat to a buoy concealing a projector, where they are trapped on the buoy by a magnet and targeted by torpedoes.
They use a radio-detonator to destroy two of the torpedoes, and a porpoise sacrifices itself to intercept the last one.

The villainess, disguised as a Soviet journalist, helps the group kidnap a man and pretends to be kidnapped with him, as part of a plot to lure the hero and finish him off with another of the villain's explosive animals (of course, unaware that the man is the hero's alter-ego).
After the man fights his way out of captivity, he again disguises himself as the hero, and the duo returns to the alliance's HQ, only to find a smoking bomb.
The hero is met with frustration, rushing all over the docks, unable to locate a safe place to dispose of the bomb, but finally does so in the nick of time.
The villain disguises himself as the commodore and schemes his way into the hidden base along with five dehydrated henchmen.

This plan fails when the henchmen unexpectedly disappear into antimatter once struck: the villain mistakenly rehydrates them with toxic heavy water used to recharge the hidden base's atomic pile, leaving them highly unstable.
Ultimately, the hero and his sidekick are unable to prevent the kidnapping of the dehydrated security council of a world organization, consisting of ambassadors from nine nations.

Giving chase in the boat to retrieve them (and the journalist, presumed by the duo as still captive), the sidekick uses a sonic charge weapon to disable the villain's submarine and force it to surface, where a fist fight ensues.
Although the hero and his sidekick come out on top, the hero is heartbroken to discover that his "true love," the journalist, is actually the villainess when she loses her mask.
The commodore accidentally breaks the powdered council members' vials and sneezes on them, scattering the dust.
The hero sets to work, constructing an elaborate super molecular dust separator to filter the mingled dust.
The sidekick asks him whether it might be in the world's best interests for them to alter the dust samples so that humans can no longer harm one another.

In response, the hero says that they cannot do so, reminding the sidekick of the fate of the villain's henchmen and their tainted rehydration, and can only hope for people, in general, to learn to live together peacefully on their own.
With the world watching, the security council is re-hydrated.

All members are restored alive and well, but continue to squabble amongst themselves, totally oblivious of their surroundings; however, each of them now speaks the language and displays the stereotypical mannerisms of a nation other than their own.
The hero quietly expresses his sincere hope to the sidekick that this "strange mixing of minds" does more good than harm.
The duo quietly leaves the organization's headquarters by climbing out of the window and descending on their ropes.
Over a decade after an international body outlawed superheroes and the villain murdered the vigilante's protégé, a 55-year-old billionaire battles alcoholism in a dystopian 1986.
Having long abandoned his mantle, he remains deeply estranged from the protégé's predecessor.
The vigilante's absence has left the city overrun by crime, much of it driven by a gang.
Haunted by his parents' murder and spurred by the gang's escalating crimes, the billionaire ends his retirement to return to his role as vigilante.
After thwarting multiple assaults—including one on a young girl—he targets the gang, whose leader publicly vows to kill him personally.
The vigilante's return is reported on the news, prompting the villain to awaken from catatonia at the asylum.
The vigilante foils a group of criminals working for a former villain.
Previously known by an alias, the former villain underwent extensive therapy and plastic surgery to reenter society before disappearing.
The vigilante informs the close-to-retirement police commissioner that the former villain may be planning a larger scheme.
Soon after, the former villain announces his intention to hold the city ransom with a bomb.
The vigilante defeats the former villain, whose psyche has now completely warped into his criminal persona.
At the presidential residence, the superhero and the president discuss the vigilante's actions, with the latter suggesting he may have to be arrested.
In the city, the girl, inspired by the vigilante, buys an imitation sidekick costume and searches for him.
The vigilante attacks the gang at the city dump with his car, but the gang leader goads him into a hand-to-hand fight and beats the vigilante to near-death.
The girl creates a diversion that allows her and the vigilante to retreat to the hidden base, where the billionaire's butler tends to his wounds.
Impressed with her bravery, the billionaire decides to make the girl his new protégée.

The vigilante returns to strategically defeat the gang leader in front of his followers, who splinter into smaller gangs as a result; one faction renames itself after the vigilante and adopts violent tactics against the underworld.

The superhero talks with the billionaire and is then deployed by the government to a fictional Latin American country, where he fights Soviet combat forces in a conflict that may escalate into a third world war.
The police commissioner's successor, a captain, declares the vigilante a wanted criminal.
Meanwhile, the villain manipulates his caretakers to allow him onto a television talk show, where he murders everyone with his trademark toxin and escapes.
The vigilante and his sidekick (the girl) track him to a county fair while evading a city police pursuit.
The vigilante fights the villain, vowing to stop him permanently.
The vigilante paralyzes the villain but stops short of taking his life.
Disappointed with the vigilante's refusal to kill him, the villain breaks his own neck and dies.
A citywide manhunt for the vigilante begins.

Elsewhere, the superhero diverts a Soviet nuclear warhead which detonates in a desert, nearly killing him in the process, and survives only by absorbing the sun's energy from the plants in a nearby jungle.
The country is hit by an electromagnetic pulse as a result and descends into chaos during the following blackout.
In the city, the vigilante and his sidekick turn the remaining gang members and the faction named after the vigilante into a non-lethal vigilante gang, making the city the safest city in the country.
Embarrassed, the government orders the superhero to take the vigilante into custody.
The superhero demands to meet the vigilante, and the billionaire chooses an alley.
The superhero tries to reason with the vigilante, but the vigilante uses his technological inventions to fight him on equal ground.
During the battle, the superhero compromises the vigilante's exoframe.
However, an aging archer manages to shoot the superhero with a green-rock-tipped arrow to weaken him, which allows the vigilante to beat him into submission.
Standing over the defeated superhero, the vigilante has a sudden heart attack, apparently dying.
The butler destroys the hidden base and the manor before suffering a fatal stroke, exposing the vigilante as the billionaire, whose fortune has disappeared.
After the billionaire's funeral, it is revealed that his death was staged using an antiarrhythmic agent that suspended his vital life signs.
The superhero attends the funeral and winks at the disguised girl after hearing the billionaire's heartbeat before she starts digging him out.
Some time afterward, the billionaire, now looking forward to life, leads his sidekick, the archer, and the rest of his followers into the caverns beyond the hidden base to continue his war on crime.
A billionaire returns home to the city after twelve years abroad, training for a one-man war against crime.
A policeman moves to the city with his pregnant wife after a transfer from another city.

Both are already acquainted with the corrupt and violent atmosphere of the city, but because the policeman assaulted a corrupt officer without obtaining evidence, he is so disgraced that no other police force will take him.
The policeman focuses on purging corruption from the city police department after witnessing his partner abuse his power.
Several officers led by the partner beat him on orders from his superior, the police commissioner, and threaten to do the same to his wife if he continues cracking down on corruption.
In revenge, the policeman tracks the partner down, beats him, and leaves him naked and handcuffed in the snow.
The billionaire believes he is still unprepared to fight crime despite the skills he learned abroad.
He goes in disguise on a surveillance mission in the city's red-light district but is drawn into a brawl with several prostitutes.
Police officers shoot the billionaire and take him away in their patrol car.
The billionaire breaks free, subdues the cops, flees from the scene, and returns to his manor barely alive.
He sits before his father's bust, requesting guidance in his war against crime.
A bat crashes through a window and settles on the bust, inspiring the billionaire to save the city as a vigilante.
The policeman diffuses a hostage situation without any deaths or injuries, leading the press to hail him as a hero, which inhibits the commissioner and his cronies from acting against him.
With the billionaire striking as the vigilante, street crime significantly declines.
The partner is attacked while accepting a bribe from a drug dealer of a crime boss.
The policeman becomes obsessed with apprehending the vigilante.
The vigilante infiltrates the mansion of the city's mayor and threatens all the dinner party guests, including the commissioner and the crime boss.
The policeman and a police sergeant witness the vigilante save an old lady from a runaway truck and summon more police officers to the scene, forcing the vigilante to flee into an abandoned building.
The commissioner personally deploys in a police helicopter and drops bombs onto the building.
A SWAT team led by a trigger-happy commander is sent in to continue the manhunt.
The vigilante uses a signal device to attract a swarm of bats from the hidden base, concealing his escape.
The policeman and the sergeant have an affair for two months, before the policeman finally ends it out of guilt.
Weeks later he confesses the affair to his wife.
The policeman apprehends the dealer, but the vigilante persuades the assistant district attorney to let him out on bail.
The vigilante uses the opportunity to terrorize the dealer into testifying against the partner.
The billionaire sneaks into the crime boss's manor as the vigilante and overhears a conversation between the crime boss and his nephew.

An attack by one of the prostitutes, now a professional burglar, interrupts before he can record any useful evidence, but he hears enough to surmise the crime boss and the nephew intend to target the policeman's family.
The policeman leaves home on the commissioner's orders but becomes suspicious when he spots the billionaire entering his home parking lot on a motorcycle at high speed.
The policeman turns back, to discover the nephew and his men holding his wife and their newborn son hostage.
With sleep deprivation causing the policeman to be paranoid and abnormally violent, he opens fire on the nephew's men.
The nephew flees the scene with the baby.
The billionaire tries to intervene, but the policeman shoots him and takes the motorcycle to chase the nephew.
The policeman and the nephew fight on a bridge until the baby falls.
The billionaire catches up on a stolen bicycle, leaps over the bridge's railing, and saves the baby.
The policeman, unable to identify the billionaire due to losing his glasses in the fight, lets him go.
The partner supplies the assistant district attorney with the evidence and testimony needed to implicate the commissioner, who resigns in disgrace.
The policeman is promoted to captain and prepares to meet with the vigilante to investigate a plot orchestrated by a criminal calling himself by an alias.
An unnamed man quits his job at a chemical company to become a stand-up comedian, only to fail miserably.
Desperate to support his pregnant wife, he agrees to guide two criminals through the chemical plant where he previously worked so that they can rob the playing card company next to it.
The police inform him that his wife and unborn child have died in a household accident.
Grief-stricken, the comedian tries to withdraw from the plan, but the criminals convince him into keeping his commitment.
At the plant, the criminals encounter security personnel, and a shootout ensues in which the comedian's two accomplices are killed.
The comedian is then confronted by the hero.
He flees by jumping into the chemical plant's waste pound lock and is swept through a pipe leading outside.
He discovers to his shock that the chemicals have permanently bleached his skin chalk-white, stained his lips red and dyed his hair green.
His disfigurement, compounded by the loss of his family, drives him completely insane and marks the birth of the villain.
He later admits that he is not sure whether this actually happened, as he tends to remember his past differently at different times.
In present day, the hero goes to the asylum to talk with the villain about ending their years-long feud, only to find that the villain has escaped.
The villain shoots and paralyzes a woman and kidnaps her father, the police commissioner.
He takes the commissioner to an abandoned amusement park, where he tortures and cages him in the park's freak show.
He forces the commissioner to view blown-up photos of his wounded daughter, lying stripped nude and in pain on the floor after the shooting.
He then puts the commissioner on display before the park's freaks, ridiculing him as "the average man", a weakling doomed to insanity.
The hero's attempts to locate the police commissioner are unsuccessful until the villain sends him an invitation to the amusement park.
Though traumatized by his ordeal, the commissioner retains his sanity and moral code, and insists that the hero capture the villain "by the book" to "show him that our way works".

The hero dodges a series of booby traps while the villain tries to persuade his nemesis that the world is a "black, awful joke" that is not worth fighting for, and it only takes "one bad day" to drive an ordinary man insane.
The hero subdues the villain and tells him that the commissioner is as sane as ever, and the villain is alone in his madness.
He offers to help the villain rehabilitate in order to end their everlasting war, which the hero fears may one day result in a fight to the death.
The villain apologetically declines, saying it is too late for that.
He says that the situation reminds him of a joke about two inmates in an asylum who try to escape.
The hero chuckles at the joke's punchline, and as the two old foes share a laugh, he grabs the villain as police arrive.
While eavesdropping on a child pornography ring and awaiting police backup in the city, the sidekick ignores the hero's orders and attacks the criminals.
The hero chastises the sidekick and asks if he considers crimefighting a game; the sidekick replies that life is a game.
At the manor, the hero decides the sidekick is emotionally unstable and relieves him of his duties as sidekick; the enraged sidekick storms off.
Meanwhile, the villain escapes from the asylum.
The hero discovers that he has obtained a nuclear weapon and plans to sell it to terrorists, and tracks him to a war-torn country.
Walking through his old neighborhood, the sidekick meets a friend of his late parents, who gives him his father's old documents.
The sidekick discovers that his mother's name on his birth certificate is blotted out.
Her first initial is "S", not "C" as in the name of the woman he knew as his mother.
The sidekick concludes that this woman was his stepmother and decides to search for his biological mother.
He uses the computer to track three possible individuals to two foreign regions.
The sidekick travels to the war-torn country, where he and the hero reunite.
The two foil an attempt by terrorists to destroy a city using the nuclear missile purchased from the villain.
The hero agrees to help the sidekick find his mother, and the sidekick interrogates his first suspect, an intelligence agent.
His next suspect, the hero's old acquaintance, says she is not the sidekick's mother after she is administered a truth serum by the duo.
The hero and the sidekick travel to another country and confirm that the sidekick's mother is an aid worker; the sidekick has an emotional reunion with her.
However, the villain discovers that the sidekick's mother had performed illegal surgeries on teenagers in the city and has been blacklisted as a medical practitioner.
He blackmails her into giving him the medical supplies her agency has stockpiled in a warehouse.
He sells them on the black market and stocks the warehouse with his venom, which will kill thousands of people.
The sidekick witnesses the villain blackmail his mother, so he reveals his identity as the hero's sidekick to her and offers to help.
The sidekick's mother rebuffs him, as she has been embezzling from the aid agency; in an attempt to cover this up, she hands the sidekick over to the villain.
The villain beats the sidekick with a crowbar and restrains him and his mother in the warehouse with a time bomb.
The sidekick throws himself on the bomb to protect his mother as the warehouse explodes.
The hero arrives too late to save them, and the sidekick and his mother die from their injuries.
Traumatized, the hero takes the sidekick and his mother's remains to the city and holds a burial with the butler, the police commissioner, and the commissioner's daughter.
The hero blames himself for the sidekick's death and resolves to carry on alone, rejecting the butler's suggestion to involve his first sidekick.
An ayatollah approaches the villain and offers him a role in the Iranian government.
The villain leaves a warehouse containing the corpses of his henchmen and the address of an international body's headquarters for the hero.
As the hero waits outside the international body's building, another hero appears and tries to convince the hero to leave.

The villain is the country's representative to the international body and will be giving a speech on the floor of the general assembly, and any confrontation between the hero and him could start a diplomatic incident.
During his speech, the villain attempts to poison the chamber with his venom, but the other hero intercepts it.
The hero pursues the villain onto a helicopter sent by his sponsors.
During the resulting struggle, one of the villain's henchmen opens fire with a machine gun and shoots the pilot, crashing the helicopter into the sea.
The other hero saves the hero, but the villain disappears.
The hero laments that everything between him and the villain ends unresolved.
In a Victorian-era city, the hero saves a wealthy couple from being robbed by three orphans and defeats their abusive handler.
At the same time, an orphan turned exotic dancer and prostitute becomes the newest victim of the serial killer who preys on the city's poor and destitute women.
Citizens of the city believe the hero and the killer to be the same man.
A famed local actress berates the police commissioner and the chief of police for their failure to stop the serial murders.
At the theatre with his friend, the district attorney, the gentleman meets the actress and the two bond at the exclusive club.
The gentleman realizes that not only were the two of them raised by a nun, but that some of the murdered girls were orphans formerly under the nun's care.
The gentleman realizes that the killer will target the nun and rushes to save her but is too late.
At the crime scene, the gentleman finds a bloody club pin, meaning the killer has to be one of the city's wealthy.
At the nun's funeral, the gentleman is met by a psychiatrist, claiming he knows the killer and wants to meet with the hero.
The gentleman also is met by a drunken old woman who claims she saw him sneaking around when the nun was killed.
At the asylum, the killer ambushes the psychiatrist and throws him to his own frenzied patients, who tear him apart.
While in pursuit of the killer, the hero is himself chased by police, only to be saved by the costumed actress.
After seeing the hero is the gentleman, she takes him to her home, where they spend the night.
After the old woman is found dead, the gentleman is arrested, and the district attorney, jealous of the actress's affection, prosecutes him as the killer.
Sentenced to a penitentiary following the trial, the gentleman is met by the actress, who urges him to reveal he is the hero to clear his name and help save the girls from the killer.
When he refuses, she decides to tell the commissioner herself.
Bribing a guard to deliver a coded message to his manor, the gentleman escapes after staging a prison fight.
The actress meets with the commissioner at the city's world's fair and learns to her horror that he is the killer.
While seeking the actress at the commissioner's home, the hero learns this as well.
The commissioner injects the actress with a sleeping aid, but she remains conscious long enough to give the hero a signal using her blood on a searchlight.

The hero arrives and fights the commissioner into a Ferris wheel where the commissioner, driven insane by his time in the civil war, reveals his "holy work" is to rid the city from what he sees as human filth.
The Ferris wheel lights on fire in the struggle and begins to collapse: the hero defeats the commissioner, who chooses to commit suicide.
The hero and the actress are saved by his ally and the orphans, who are now the gentleman's wards.

On April 1, the police commissioner informs the hero that the patients of the asylum, led by the villain, have taken over the facility, threatening to murder the staff unless the hero agrees to meet with them.
Among the hostages are the asylum's administrator and a therapist.

At the asylum, the hero discovers that one patient's mental condition has deteriorated as a result of the therapist's therapy; she replaced the patient's trademark coin with a six-sided die, then a tarot deck, increasing the number of choices he has in the hope that he will eventually not leave any of his choices up to chance.
Instead, the treatment renders him incapable of making even the simplest decisions, such as going to the bathroom.
The villain forces the hero into a game of hide and seek, giving him one hour to escape the asylum before his adversaries are sent to hunt him down.
Through the asylum, the hero encounters six of his adversaries.
He reaches a secret room in the towers, where he finds the administrator holding the therapist hostage.
It is revealed that the administrator orchestrated the riots, and has the hero read the diary of the asylum's founder when questioned why.
In flashbacks, it is shown that the founder's mentally ill mother suffered delusions of being tormented by a supernatural entity.
After believing to have seen the creature himself (a bat), the founder killed her to end her suffering.
He blocked out the memory, only to have it return after an inmate raped and murdered the founder's wife and daughter.
Traumatized, the founder vowed to bind the evil spirit of "the bat" with sorcery.
He killed the inmate during a shock therapy session and continued his mission even after he was incarcerated in his own asylum, up until his death.
The administrator came to believe that he was destined to continue the founder's work.
On April Fools' Day (the date the founder's family was murdered), the administrator released the patients and lured the hero to the asylum, believing him to be the bat the founder spoke of.
He accuses the hero of feeding the evil of the asylum by bringing it more insane souls and they fight, which ends when the therapist slashes the administrator's throat to save the hero.
The hero breaks down the front door of the asylum, proclaiming that the inmates are now free.
He returns the patient's coin to him, stating that it should be up to him to decide his fate at the hands of the inmates.
The patient declares that they will kill the hero if the coin lands scratched side up and let him go if the unscarred side lands.
He flips the coin and declares the hero free.
As the villain bids the hero goodbye, the inmates return to their cells and the police arrive to retake the asylum.
The patient looks at the coin and it is revealed that it actually landed scratched side up, implying that he made his own choice.
He turns to the stack of tarot cards and knocks them over, reciting a passage from a book: "Who cares for you?
You're nothing but a pack of cards".
A newspaper reporter and a photojournalist investigate sightings of a masked vigilante targeting the city's criminals.
Both attend a fundraiser hosted by a billionaire, who is secretly the vigilante, having chosen this path after witnessing a mugger murder his parents when he was a child.
During the event, the billionaire becomes attracted to the photojournalist.
Meanwhile, a mob boss sends his sociopathic second-in-command to break into a chemical plant and retrieve incriminating evidence.
However, this is secretly a ploy to have the second-in-command murdered for carrying on an affair with the mob boss's mistress.
A corrupt city police lieutenant arranges the hit on the second-in-command by conducting an unauthorized raid on the chemical plant.
However, the police commissioner learns of the raid and takes command, ordering the officers to capture the second-in-command alive.
The vigilante also appears, while the second-in-command shoots and kills the lieutenant as revenge for the double-cross.
During a scuffle with the vigilante, the second-in-command topples off a catwalk and falls into a vat of chemicals.
Although presumed dead, the second-in-command survives with various disfigurements including chalk white skin and emerald-green hair and nails.
He undergoes surgery to repair the damage, but ends up with a rictus grin.
Driven insane by his hideous appearance, the second-in-command, now calling himself by an alias, kills the mob boss, massacres the mob boss's associates, and takes over his operations.
The villain begins terrorizing the city by lacing various hygiene products with a drug – a deadly chemical that causes victims to die laughing.
The villain soon becomes obsessed with the photojournalist and lures her to a museum, which his henchmen vandalize.
The vigilante rescues the photojournalist, takes her to the hidden base, and provides her with all of his research on the drug, which will allow the city's residents to escape the toxin.
Conflicted with his love for her, the billionaire visits her apartment intending to reveal his secret identity, only for the villain to interrupt the meeting.
The villain asks the billionaire, "Have you ever danced with the devil in the pale moonlight?", which the billionaire recognizes as the phrase used by the mugger who murdered his parents.
He shoots the billionaire, who survives by hiding a serving tray underneath his shirt.
The photojournalist is taken to the hidden base by the billionaire's butler, who had been coaxing the relationship between the pair.
After the photojournalist learns his secret, the billionaire chooses to battle the villain for the sake of the city over their relationship.
He then departs to destroy the chemical plant used to create the drug.
Meanwhile, the villain lures the city's citizens to a parade honoring the city's bicentennial with the promise of free money.
This turns out to be a trap designed to dose them with the drug in gas form, held within giant parade balloons.
The vigilante foils his plan by using his aircraft to remove the balloons, but the villain shoots him down.
The aircraft crashes in front of a cathedral, which the villain uses to take the photojournalist hostage.
The vigilante pursues the villain, and in the ensuing fight, he identifies the villain killed his parents and thus, indirectly created the vigilante.

The villain eventually pulls the vigilante and the photojournalist over the cathedral's roof, leaving them hanging while he calls for a helicopter piloted by his goons, who throw down a ladder for him to climb.
The vigilante uses a grappling hook to attach the villain's leg to a crumbling gargoyle that eventually falls off the roof.
Unable to bear the statue's immense weight, the villain falls to his death while the vigilante and the photojournalist make it to safety.
Sometime later, the commissioner announces that the police have arrested all of the villain's men, effectively dismantling the remains of the mob boss's organizations, and unveils the signal light.
The vigilante leaves the police a note, promising to defend the city should crime strike again, and asking them to use the signal light to summon him in times of need.
The butler takes the photojournalist to the manor, explaining that the billionaire will be a little late.
She responds that she is not surprised, as the vigilante looks at the signal's projection from a rooftop, standing watch over the city.
In the city, two wealthy socialites, horrified by the birth of their malformed and feral son, abandon him in the sewers, where a colony of penguins takes him in.

Thirty-three years later, during the Christmas season, a wealthy industrialist is abducted by a gang—former circus performers implicated in child disappearances across the country—and taken to their hideout in the abandoned arctic exhibit at the city zoo.

Their leader, the abandoned son, now known by an alias, blackmails the industrialist with evidence of his corruption and murders, coercing him into helping the villain re-enter the city's high society.
The industrialist stages the kidnapping of the mayor's infant child, allowing the villain to "rescue" the child and become a public hero.
In return, the villain requests access to the city's birth records, claiming he seeks to uncover his true identity by investigating the city's first-born sons.
The industrialist attempts to kill his timid secretary by pushing her out of a window after she discovers his plan to build a power plant that would secretly drain and store the city's electricity.
The secretary survives, returns home, crafts a costume, and adopts a new persona.
To the industrialist's surprise, she reappears at work with newfound confidence and assertiveness, immediately attracting the attention of a visiting billionaire.
As the vigilante, the billionaire begins investigating the villain, suspecting his ties to the gang.
Seeking to remove opposition to his power plant, the industrialist convinces the villain to run for mayor and discredit the incumbent by unleashing the gang on the city.
The vigilante's efforts to quell the violence bring him into conflict with the costumed woman, while in their civilian lives the secretary and the billionaire begin a romance.
Meanwhile, the costumed woman allies with the villain to smear the vigilante's reputation.
During the city's Christmas-tree lighting, the villain and the costumed woman kidnap the city's beauty queen and lure the vigilante to a rooftop above the ceremony.
The villain pushes the beauty queen to her death with a swarm of bats, framing the vigilante.
When the costumed woman objects to the murder and rebuffs the villain's sexual advances, he attacks her, sending her crashing through a glasshouse.
The vigilante escapes in his car, unaware that the gang has sabotaged it, allowing the villain to take it on a remote-controlled rampage.

Before regaining control, the vigilante records the villain's insulting tirade against the city's citizens and later plays it during the villain's mayoral rally, destroying his public image and forcing him to retreat to the city zoo.
There, the villain renounces his humanity, fully embracing his alias, and sets his plan in motion to abduct and kill the city's first-born sons as revenge for his own abandonment.
The secretary attempts to kill the industrialist at his charity ball, but the billionaire intervenes, and the two inadvertently discover each other's secret identities.
The villain crashes the event intending to kidnap the industrialist's son, but the industrialist offers himself instead.
The vigilante disrupts the gang and halts the kidnappings, prompting the villain to unleash his missile-equipped penguin army to destroy the city.
The vigilante's ally overrides the control signal, redirecting the penguins back to the city zoo.
As the missiles obliterate the zoo, the vigilante unleashes a swarm of bats, causing the villain to fall into the toxic waters of the arctic exhibit.
The costumed woman confronts the industrialist, rejecting the vigilante's plea to abandon her revenge and leave with him.
The industrialist shoots the vigilante, incapacitating him, and then shoots the costumed woman multiple times, but she survives, claiming she has two of her nine lives left.
The costumed woman electrocutes the industrialist with a live cable, causing a power surge that appears to kill them both; however, the vigilante finds only the industrialist's charred remains.
The villain emerges one last time but succumbs to his injuries, with his penguins carrying his body into the water.
Sometime later, while traveling home, the billionaire spots the secretary's silhouette but finds only a cat, which he takes with him.
The signal light shines above the city as the costumed woman gazes up at it.
